lenses.sp: Wants a large, steady, cheap company with a strong balance sheet.
lenses.vd: In Benjamin Graham's spirit: would see a mixed picture (2 checks use fewer years than the rule needs).

ch.r: Market value above ₹5,000 crore
ch.w: Graham avoided small companies; ₹5,000 crore is our Indian translation of 'adequate size'.

ch.r: Current assets ÷ current liabilities ≥ 2
ch.w: For every ₹100 it owes within a year, it holds ₹132 of cash, stock and dues coming in.

ch.r: Long-term debt ≤ current assets − current liabilities
ch.v: Long-term debt ₹55 cr vs working capital ₹1,048 cr
ch.w: Graham wanted the short-term cushion alone to be able to repay long-term loans.

ch.n: A profit every year for 10 years
ch.r: Positive earnings in each of the last 10 years
ch.v: Profit in all 4 yrs we have
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see; the earlier years are not in the free data.

ch.r: Dividends every year for 20 years (India: 10 years)
ch.w: A gap of about 53 months without a dividend (2016-11 to 2021-03).

ch.n: Earnings per share up a third in 10 years
ch.r: EPS +33% over 10 years (3-year averages at each end)
ch.w: EPS (average of the first 2 vs last 2 years we have) moved +49%.

ch.r: PE ≤ 15 on 3-year average earnings
ch.w: You pay ₹27 for every ₹1 of average yearly profit over the last 3 yrs.
You pay ₹3.61 for every ₹1 of net worth.

ch.r: Price < √(22.5 × EPS × book value per share)
ch.w: With EPS ₹10.6 and book value ₹70 per share, Graham's ceiling price is ₹129.

lenses.st: Wonderful business at a fair price

ch.r: Could you explain how it makes money in two sentences?

ch.r: A lasting edge: brand, low cost, network or switching costs

Has it kept high returns through bad years?

ch.r: ROE ≥ 15% in at least 8 of the last 10 years, with debt-to-equity < 0.5
ch.w: Strong in 2 of the 4 yrs we can see.

ch.r: No loss in 10 years
ch.w: No loss in the years we can see.

ch.n: Doesn't eat its cash in capex
ch.r: Capex < 50% of operating cash flow (5-year sum)

ch.r: Share count up no more than 5% over the years we have

ch.r: Candid, sensible with capital, no governance red flags

ch.n: Bought with a margin of safety

ch.w: Needs the fair-value (DCF) estimate, which arrives in Stage 4.

ch.r: PEG (PE ÷ EPS growth) below 2

ch.r: Promoters own ≥ 25% and have pledged none

lenses.st: Growth at a reasonable price · type: Fast grower

ch.r: Debt-to-equity below 0.35
ch.w: ₹0 borrowed for every ₹100 of shareholders' money.

ch.r: EPS growth 20–25% a year

ch.r: Inventory should not grow faster than sales

ch.r: Earnings yield (EBIT ÷ EV) in the top 30%

story.what_it_does: RailTel is a government-owned telecom and IT services company. It reports an order book of ₹10166 Cr, and for FY26 up to Q3 it showed total income of ₹3551 Cr and profit after tax of ₹300 Cr.
story.plans: The deck says edge data centres at Chandigarh, Indore and Vizag are to be operational on 3 October 2026. Phase 1 of the 10MW NOIDA data centre (5 MW) is to be completed on 5 May 2027.
story.moat: The notes do not describe a specific competitive advantage. The only related fact is that it is government-owned, and the notes do not say what that means for its business.

scenarios.story: The large order book of ₹10166 Cr converts into revenue, and growth continues near the 35% income and 22% profit rise seen up to Q3 FY26. The data centre projects also open on schedule.
signals_to_watch: Order book of ₹10166 Cr being converted into income
Edge data centres operational by 3 October 2026

scenarios.story: Income and profit keep growing, but profit grows more slowly than income, as in FY26 up to Q3 (22% vs 35%). The data centre builds proceed over the stated timelines.
signals_to_watch: Profit after tax growth versus total income growth
Phase 1 of the NOIDA data centre by 5 May 2027

scenarios.story: Profit growth lags income growth further, and the data centre timelines slip. The deck gives no net debt, capex or EBITDA, so cash strain could go unnoticed.
signals_to_watch: Disclosure of net debt, capex or EBITDA, which the deck does not state
Any delay to the data centre dates of 3 October 2026 or 5 May 2027
